proposed.explanation:
The evidence you provided is for a company called COMI (ticker COMI), not for CIB (Commercial International Bank). Because the financial data—net profit, EPS, equity, and customer liabilities—belongs to COMI, I cannot use it to assess whether CIB is a suitable investment. I therefore cannot give a responsible buy/hold/sell recommendation on CIB shares.

What is missing: CIB's own income statement, balance sheet, EPS, dividend history, and any valuation metrics (P/E, P/B) for the most recent reporting period. Without CIB-specific figures I cannot compare its earnings growth, profitability, or valuation to the 128 EGP price you would pay.

A separate but important point: even if the evidence were for CIB, putting the entire 200,000 EGP into a single stock would concentrate all of your investment capital in one company. With a medium willingness to accept losses and a 5-year horizon, a single-stock position exposes you to company-specific risk (regulatory changes, management decisions, sector shocks) that a diversified portfolio would spread. A prudent approach would be to allocate only a portion of the bonus to any one stock and keep the remainder in other instruments or cash until you have a broader view.

I recommend obtaining CIB's latest audited or condensed financial statements and, if possible, a peer comparison before deciding how much (if any) of the 200,000 EGP to allocate to CIB shares.
